About This Book
内容简介

Generative AI is revolutionizing industries, and Kubernetes has fast become the backbone for deploying and managing these resource-intensive workloads. This book serves as a practical, hands-on guide for MLOps engineers, software developers, Kubernetes administrators, and AI professionals ready to combine AI innovation with the power of cloud native infrastructure. Authors Roland Huß and Daniele Zonca provide a clear road map for deploying, fine-tuning, and scaling large models on Kubernetes to power AI-driven applications, addressing challenges like GPU resource optimization, observability, and security along the way. With actionable insights and real-world examples, readers will learn to tackle the opportunities and complexities of managing GenAI applications in production environments. Whether you’re experimenting with large language models (LLMs) or facing the nuances of AI deployment at scale, you’ll uncover the expertise you need to operationalize this exciting technology effectively.

生成式 AI 正在变革各行各业，而 Kubernetes 已迅速成为部署与管理这些资源密集型工作负载的骨干。本书是一本实操指南，面向 MLOps 工程师、软件开发人员、Kubernetes 管理员以及准备把 AI 创新与云原生基础设施之力结合起来的 AI 从业者。作者 Roland Huß 与 Daniele Zonca 给出了清晰的路线图，讲解如何在 Kubernetes 上部署、微调和扩展大模型以驱动 AI 应用，并沿途应对 GPU 资源优化、可观测性与安全等挑战。凭借可落地的洞见与真实示例，读者将学会在生产环境中驾驭 GenAI 应用的机遇与复杂性。无论你是在试验大语言模型（LLM），还是在面对大规模 AI 部署的种种微妙之处，都能从中获得有效运营这项激动人心技术所需的专业知识。

Preface
前言

The end of 2022 marked a turning point in the world of AI with the release of ChatGPT, a chat-based language model designed to generate human-like text in response to conversational input. We all witnessed an AI revolution that transformed our expectations and possibilities. Generative AI models have been around for a while. In fact, deep learning concepts have existed for decades, but it’s only with the recent availability of large amounts of data and advances in accelerators and compute power that this AI revolution finally became possible. This, combined with a massive increase in model parameters reaching billions, has brought about a remarkable shift. Imagine a phase transition in physics: the same substance suddenly exhibits completely new properties. That’s what happened with AI, revealing new capabilities that were previously unimaginable, such as advanced natural language processing (NLP) and the ability to generate coherent and contextual responses. Small steps in AI development led to significant impacts, as we have seen over the past few years when interest in generative AI models and their diverse applications has exploded. While this early pioneering era is exciting, it is also extremely demanding.

2022 年底，ChatGPT 的发布标志着 AI 世界的一个转折点——这是一个基于对话的语言模型，能针对对话式输入生成类人文本。我们都目睹了一场 AI 革命，它改变了我们的期待与可能。生成式 AI 模型其实已经存在一段时间了。事实上，深度学习概念已有数十年历史，但直到近年来海量数据可得、加速器与算力进步，这场 AI 革命才终于成为现实。再加上模型参数规模跃升至数十亿，带来了非凡的转变。想象物理学中的相变：同一种物质突然展现出全新性质。AI 正是如此，显露出此前难以想象的能力，比如高级自然语言处理（NLP）以及生成连贯、贴合语境回复的能力。正如过去几年我们所见，AI 发展中的每一小步都带来了巨大影响，业界对生成式 AI 模型及其多样应用的兴趣呈爆发式增长。这个早期开拓时代既激动人心，也极其考验人。

As of early 2026, you can find millions of generative AI models on the Hugging Face Hub, the central repository of the AI community, for various applications. Once you choose a model, the main question for application developers and Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) engineers is how to operate these models in production systems. Nonfunctional aspects such as resilience, scalability, security, and above all, operational cost, are paramount. The challenge of bringing a model from experimentation (such as a Jupyter Notebook) into production is not trivial. Fortunately, a distributed software platform has emerged in recent years to manage various types of workloads in a scalable and resilient manner: Kubernetes.

截至 2026 年初，你可以在 Hugging Face Hub（AI 社区的中心仓库）上找到数百万个面向各种应用的生成式 AI 模型。一旦选定模型，应用开发者与机器学习运维（MLOps）工程师面临的主要问题就是：如何在生产系统中运营这些模型。弹性、可扩展性、安全，尤其是运维成本等非功能属性至关重要。把模型从实验阶段（比如 Jupyter Notebook）搬进生产并非易事。幸运的是，近年来出现了一个分布式软件平台，可弹性、稳健地管理各类工作负载：Kubernetes。

When Kubernetes was introduced in 2014, generative AI was still a distant concept. Kubernetes initially excelled as a platform for stateless (web) applications and microservices, but it has evolved into a reliable foundation for running stateful applications such as databases and messaging systems. A similar evolution is underway for the specific requirements of large language models (LLMs) with their enormous data structures and special hardware needs.

Kubernetes 于 2014 年推出时，生成式 AI 还是个遥远的概念。Kubernetes 最初以无状态（Web）应用与微服务平台见长，但已演进为运行数据库、消息系统等有状态应用的可靠基石。如今，针对大语言模型（LLM）巨大的数据结构与特殊硬件需求，一场类似的演进正在发生。

原书第 13 页

This book examines the various challenges and solutions for operating generative AI in general and LLMs in particular.

本书考察运营生成式 AI（尤其是 LLM）所面临的种种挑战与解决方案。

Why We Wrote This Book
我们为什么写这本书

Our motivation to write this book stems from the growing need to bridge the gap between Kubernetes experts and the emerging demands of running LLM production. As LLMs have become increasingly essential in various industries, the challenge is no longer just about developing these models but also about deploying, scaling, and maintaining them effectively in real-world production environments.

我们写这本书的动机，源于弥合 Kubernetes 专家与 LLM 生产运营新需求之间鸿沟的迫切需要。随着 LLM 在各行各业日益关键，挑战已不再只是开发这些模型，还包括在真实生产环境中有效部署、扩缩容与维护它们。

We approach LLM workloads as black boxes by acknowledging their operational complexity without requiring the deep insights of a data scientist. This perspective is crucial for Kubernetes practitioners who want to operationalize these models without delving into the details of machine learning (ML). By focusing on Kubernetes as the underlying platform, we provide practical guidance on how to use Kubernetes to meet the unique requirements of LLMs, ensuring they run efficiently, securely, and at scale.

我们把 LLM 工作负载当作黑盒来对待：承认其运维复杂性，但不要求数据科学家那样的深刻洞见。这一视角对想运营这些模型、却不愿深入机器学习（ML）细节的 Kubernetes 从业者至关重要。我们以 Kubernetes 为底层平台，给出如何用它满足 LLM 独特需求、让模型高效、安全、大规模运行的实用指导。

This book is our contribution to helping you with the challenges of operationalizing generative AI on Kubernetes, empowering you to bring LLMs and AI-driven applications into production with confidence.

本书是我们为帮助你应对在 Kubernetes 上运营生成式 AI 挑战所尽的一份力，让你有信心把 LLM 与 AI 驱动应用送上生产。

Kubernetes

Kubernetes, also referred to as K8s, is a container orchestration platform designed to automate the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications. Initially focusing on stateless applications, it has evolved to support stateful workloads such as databases and messaging systems. Today, Kubernetes stands out as the dominant operational platform for a wide array of traditional workloads, and it is increasingly pivotal in the AI domain.

Kubernetes（亦称 K8s）是一个容器编排平台，旨在自动化容器化应用的部署、扩缩容与管理。它最初聚焦无状态应用，后演进为支持数据库、消息系统等有状态工作负载。如今，Kubernetes 已是众多传统工作负载的主导运维平台，并在 AI 领域日益关键。

Several pioneering initiatives and organizations have chosen Kubernetes to power their AI workloads, benefiting from its robust scalability and resilience. For instance, companies like Google and OpenAI leverage Kubernetes to manage their complex machine learning pipelines and deployment processes.

多个开创性项目与组织选择 Kubernetes 支撑其 AI 工作负载，受益于它强大的可扩展性与弹性。例如 Google、OpenAI 等公司用 Kubernetes 管理复杂的机器学习流水线与部署流程。

Kubernetes abstracts and automates many operational aspects, such as scaling, load balancing, and self-healing. This allows developers and MLOps engineers to focus on domain-specific tasks without worrying about the underlying infrastructure. Its support for declarative configuration and infrastructure as code, which can be leveraged with GitOps, ensures consistency and reliability across deployments.

Kubernetes 抽象并自动化了扩缩容、负载均衡、自愈等许多运维环节，让开发者与 MLOps 工程师专注于领域任务而不必操心底层基础设施。它对声明式配置与基础设施即代码的支持（可配合 GitOps 使用）保证了各次部署间的一致性与可靠性。

原书第 14 页

One of Kubernetes’ most significant strengths lies in its ability to compose larger applications that encompass multiple types of workloads, including serving LLMs. While specialized platforms like Ray or Spark excel at running specific ML and AI workloads, they are purpose-built for these use cases and do not provide the same level of native integration for diverse workload types that Kubernetes offers. Kubernetes, on the other hand, can seamlessly manage AI models alongside traditional business applications, databases, and microservices. This holistic approach not only simplifies operations but also enhances the efficiency of developing and deploying complex applications that require different types of workloads to work together smoothly.

Kubernetes 最重要的优势之一，是能够把包含多种工作负载类型（包括服务 LLM）的大型应用组合起来。Ray、Spark 等专用平台虽擅长运行特定 ML/AI 工作负载，但它们是为这些用例量身打造的，无法像 Kubernetes 那样原生集成多种不同类型的工作负载。而 Kubernetes 可以把 AI 模型与传统业务应用、数据库、微服务无缝放在一起管理。这种整体思路不仅简化运维，还提升了那些需要多种工作负载协同工作的复杂应用的开发与部署效率。

Generative AI

The history of generative AI is a fascinating journey that spans several decades, marked by groundbreaking innovations and rapid technological advancements. Its roots can be traced back to the mid-20th century, with early foundations laid by pioneers like Claude E. Shannon, who introduced the concept of sequences of letters or words to predict subsequent characters in a string for text generation in 1948, and Alan Turing, whose 1950 paper proposed the famous Turing Test. The true revolution in generative AI (GenAI), however, began in the 2010s with the advent of deep learning techniques. The 2012 AlexNet breakthrough on the ImageNet dataset proved that deep neural networks could work at scale, catalyzing the broader deep learning revolution. Building on this foundation, the introduction of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) by Ian Goodfellow in 2014 marked a pivotal moment for generative AI specifically, enabling the creation of highly realistic synthetic data across various modalities. This was followed by the development of the Transformer model by Google researchers in 2017, which revolutionized natural language processing. The subsequent years saw the rapid evolution of LLMs, with OpenAI’s GPT series, particularly GPT-3 and its successors, demonstrating unprecedented capabilities in text generation, language understanding, and even code writing. The launch of ChatGPT in 2022 brought LLMs into the mainstream, sparking widespread public interest and debate about the potential and implications of this technology. As we move forward, the field continues to evolve at a breakneck pace, with ongoing advancements pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

生成式 AI 的历史是一段跨越数十年的迷人旅程，充满突破性创新与飞速的技术进步。其根源可追溯到 20 世纪中叶：Claude E. Shannon 早在 1948 年就提出用字母或词序列预测后续字符以生成文本的概念；Alan Turing 1950 年的论文提出了著名的图灵测试。但生成式 AI（GenAI）真正的革命始于 2010 年代深度学习技术的兴起。2012 年 AlexNet 在 ImageNet 数据集上的突破证明了深度神经网络可以规模化运作，催化了更广泛的深度学习革命。在此基础上，Ian Goodfellow 于 2014 年提出生成对抗网络（GAN），成为生成式 AI 的关键转折点，使得跨多种模态生成高度逼真的合成数据成为可能。随后 Google 研究者于 2017 年提出 Transformer 模型，彻底改变了自然语言处理。此后几年 LLM 快速演进，OpenAI 的 GPT 系列（尤其是 GPT-3 及其后继）在文本生成、语言理解乃至代码编写上展现出前所未有的能力。2022 年 ChatGPT 的发布让 LLM 进入主流，引发公众对这项技术潜力与影响的广泛兴趣与讨论。展望未来，该领域仍在以惊人速度演进，不断突破可能性的边界。

However, only recently have the capabilities of generative AI models reached a level where they can be offered as services for a wider audience. As a consequence, people started to think about the best way to run GenAI in general, and specifically, LLM workloads in production. The journey of bringing GenAI workloads into production has evolved significantly. Initially, AI models were deployed ad hoc, with bespoke scripts and manual processes. As the field matured, frameworks like TensorFlow Serving and tools like MLflow emerged to streamline the deployment experience. However, the operational challenges of managing these workloads at scale required more sophisticated solutions. Kubernetes, with its powerful orchestration capabilities, began to play a crucial role in managing ML workloads, providing a scalable and resilient platform for deployment. Unlike traditional ML models, LLMs require specialized infrastructure, including high-performance GPUs and distributed computing environments, to handle their size and computational demands.

然而，直到最近生成式 AI 模型的能力才达到可作为服务提供给更广泛受众的水平。因此，人们开始思考如何最好地在生产环境中运行 GenAI、尤其是 LLM 工作负载。把 GenAI 工作负载搬上生产的历程经历了显著演变。最初，AI 模型是临时部署的，靠定制脚本和手工流程。随着领域成熟，TensorFlow Serving 等框架、MLflow 等工具相继出现以简化部署。但大规模管理这些工作负载的运维挑战需要更复杂的方案。Kubernetes 凭借强大的编排能力，开始在管理 ML 工作负载中扮演关键角色，提供可扩展、有弹性的部署平台。与传统 ML 模型不同，LLM 需要专用基础设施——包括高性能 GPU 与分布式计算环境——来应对其规模与计算需求。

原书第 15 页

Deploying generative AI models, particularly LLMs, in a production environment is far from straightforward. The operational challenges are significant. Generative AI models require vast amounts of training data. After deployment, while individual inference requests typically process small amounts of data (like user prompts), some production scenarios such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or batch processing may involve handling larger datasets. Moreover, the effective usage of expensive accelerators like GPUs is critical. These rare hardware resources are essential for the performance of LLMs, and the AI workload orchestration platform must ensure context-aware scheduling to optimize their utilization, ensuring efficient and cost-effective operation.

在生产环境部署生成式 AI 模型（尤其是 LLM）远非易事，运维挑战巨大。生成式 AI 模型需要海量训练数据。部署后，虽然单次推理请求通常只处理少量数据（如用户 prompt），但某些生产场景（如检索增强生成 RAG 或批处理）可能要处理较大数据集。此外，高效利用 GPU 等昂贵加速器至关重要。这些稀缺硬件资源对 LLM 性能至关重要，AI 工作负载编排平台必须确保上下文感知的调度以优化其利用率，实现高效、高性价比的运行。

In this book, we will address these challenges and show how Kubernetes can be used to successfully deploy and manage generative AI models at scale.

本书将应对这些挑战，并展示如何用 Kubernetes 成功地大规模部署与管理生成式 AI 模型。

How This Book Is Structured
本书结构

This book guides you through operationalizing generative AI models on Kubernetes, and is organized into four parts that reflect the practical journey from initial deployment to production-scale AI applications. Whether you’re a Kubernetes practitioner encountering AI workloads for the first time, or an MLOps engineer seeking to leverage Kubernetes more effectively, you’ll find the content builds on your existing knowledge while introducing new concepts progressively.

本书带你在 Kubernetes 上运营生成式 AI 模型，分为四个部分，反映了从初次部署到生产级 AI 应用的实战路径。无论你是第一次接触 AI 工作负载的 Kubernetes 从业者，还是想更高效运用 Kubernetes 的 MLOps 工程师，内容都会在你已有知识之上逐步引入新概念。

Unlike traditional machine learning books that start with training, we begin with inference: deploying and serving pre-trained models. This reflects how most organizations adopt generative AI today. You typically start with existing foundation models rather than building from scratch, making model serving the natural entry point for bringing AI capabilities into production.

与传统 ML 书从训练讲起不同，我们从推理开始：部署并服务预训练模型。这反映了当今多数组织采用生成式 AI 的方式——通常从已有基础模型出发而非从头训练，因此模型服务就成了把 AI 能力引入生产的自然入口。

We have organized the content as follows: The book opens with the Introduction, which examines the operational challenges of running generative AI at scale and includes an optional technical primer on LLM fundamentals: tokenization, embeddings, and the two-phase inference process. This primer helps you understand operational metrics without requiring deep machine learning expertise, though you can skip it and treat LLMs as pure black boxes.

内容组织如下：本书以导言开篇，考察大规模运行生成式 AI 的运维挑战，并附一节可选的 LLM 基础技术入门：分词、嵌入与两阶段推理流程。这节入门帮你理解运维指标，而无需深厚的 ML 专业知识；你也可以跳过它，把 LLM 当作纯粹的黑盒。

随后是四个部分：

  • Part I, “Inference” establishes the foundation for deploying and serving LLMs. You’ll learn how model size, storage requirements, and initialization time create unique challenges compared to traditional workloads. These chapters cover packaging models in containers, managing multigigabyte model weights in persistent storage, and handling workloads that require minutes to become ready. The focus is on getting your first generative AI service running reliably.第一部分“推理”奠定部署与服务 LLM 的基础。你会了解模型规模、存储需求与初始化时间相比传统工作负载带来的独特挑战。这几章涵盖把模型打进容器、在持久存储中管理数 GB 级权重，以及处理需要数分钟才能就绪的工作负载。重点是让你的第一个生成式 AI 服务可靠跑起来。
  • Part II, “Production Readiness” addresses what happens after successful deployment. GPU resource management becomes critical as you learn to schedule scarce accelerators efficiently and maximize their utilization. You’ll then explore scaling strategies that account for model warm-up times, rolling updates that maintain service availability, and optimization techniques that balance performance with cost. The final chapter covers LLM observability, showing how to track metrics beyond CPU and memory: token throughput, prompt latency, inference costs, and model accuracy.第二部分“生产就绪”讨论成功部署之后发生什么。GPU 资源管理变得关键，你将学习高效调度稀缺加速器并最大化利用率。随后探讨兼顾模型预热时间的扩缩容策略、保持服务可用性的滚动更新，以及在性能与成本间取得平衡的优化技术。最后一章讲 LLM 可观测性，展示如何跟踪 CPU、内存之外的指标：token 吞吐、prompt 延迟、推理成本与模型准确率。
  • Part III, “Tuning” shifts focus to model customization. Fine-tuning adapts pre-trained models to specific domains or tasks, but introduces intense resource demands. A single tuning job may require multiple GPUs working in concert, consuming significant cluster resources. You’ll explore techniques like LoRA and PEFT that make customization more efficient, along with the operational challenges of managing tuning jobs on Kubernetes: job scheduling, quota allocation, resource management, and GPU configuration optimization.第三部分“调优”转向模型定制。微调让预训练模型适配特定领域或任务，但会带来巨大资源需求。单个调优作业可能需要多块 GPU 协同，消耗大量集群资源。你将探索 LoRA、PEFT 等让定制更高效的技术，以及在 Kubernetes 上管理调优作业的运维挑战：作业调度、配额分配、资源管理与 GPU 配置优化。
  • Part IV, “AI-Driven Apps” shows how to build complete applications around LLM services. These chapters present architectural patterns for AI-driven systems, from chat interfaces and event-driven backends to retrieval-augmented generation that enhances model responses with domain-specific knowledge. You’ll explore agentic workflows where models coordinate tool invocation and multistep reasoning, then tackle the production challenges unique to agentic systems: security, state management, observability, cost control, and reliability. The final chapter introduces protocols like MCP and A2A that standardize tool and agent communication.第四部分“AI 驱动应用”展示如何围绕 LLM 服务构建完整应用。这几章给出 AI 驱动系统的架构模式，从聊天界面、事件驱动后端，到用领域知识增强模型回答的检索增强生成。你将探索智能体工作流——模型协调工具调用与多步推理，然后应对智能体系统特有的生产挑战：安全、状态管理、可观测性、成本控制与可靠性。最后一章介绍 MCP、A2A 等标准化工具与智能体通信的协议。
原书第 17 页

Each chapter builds on concepts introduced earlier, while remaining approachable for selective reading. If you need to optimize GPU utilization immediately, jump to Chapter 3, “Kubernetes and GPUs”. If you’re architecting AI-enabled applications, Part IV, “AI-Driven Apps”, provides the patterns you need. Linear readers will find a natural progression from deployment fundamentals through production operations to advanced applications.

每章都建立在前面引入的概念之上，同时也便于跳读。如果你急需优化 GPU 利用率，可直接跳到第 3 章“Kubernetes 与 GPU”。如果你在架构 AI 应用，第四部分“AI 驱动应用”提供你需要的模式。线性阅读者则会看到从部署基础、生产运维到高级应用的自然递进。

Throughout the book, we maintain a practical operational perspective. You don’t need deep knowledge of transformer architectures or neural network mathematics, just as you don’t need to understand database internals to run PostgreSQL on Kubernetes. We treat LLMs as specialized workloads with unique requirements, showing you how to meet those requirements using platform capabilities and ecosystem tools.

全书我们都保持务实的运维视角。你不需要深入理解 Transformer 架构或神经网络数学，正如在 Kubernetes 上跑 PostgreSQL 不需要理解数据库内部原理一样。我们把 LLM 视为有独特需求的专用工作负载，展示如何用平台能力与生态工具满足这些需求。

Who This Book Is For
本书面向谁

This book is designed for MLOps practitioners, operational folks tasked with running AI workloads at scale in production, and architects who need to understand the unique architectural constraints of managing large AI workloads. The goal is to provide these professionals with practical insights and tools to operationalize generative AI effectively on Kubernetes.

本书面向 MLOps 从业者、负责在生产环境大规模运行 AI 工作负载的运维人员，以及需要理解管理大型 AI 工作负载独特架构约束的架构师。目标是为这些专业人士提供在 Kubernetes 上有效运营生成式 AI 的实用洞见与工具。

However, it’s important to clarify who might not find this book ideal. This book does not directly address data scientists focused on the algorithmic aspects of LLMs. For those interested in the mathematical foundations and detailed workings of LLMs, we recommend Generative Deep Learning by David Foster (O’Reilly, 2023). However, curious data scientists can still benefit from this book by learning how their artifacts can be run in production to serve the real world.

不过有必要说明本书不适合谁。本书不直接面向专注 LLM 算法层面的数据科学家。若你对 LLM 的数学基础与内部机理感兴趣，推荐 David Foster 的《Generative Deep Learning》（O’Reilly, 2023）。但好奇的数据科学家仍可从本书受益，了解自己产出的模型如何在生产中服务真实世界。

This book assumes you have a basic understanding of Kubernetes. It is not an introduction to Kubernetes, and some familiarity with its concepts and features is required. If you need a more comprehensive foundation, we suggest Kubernetes in Action by Marko Lukša (Manning, 2018) or Kubernetes Patterns by Bilgin Ibryam and Roland Huß (O’Reilly, 2023) for a deeper dive into Kubernetes principles and best practices.

本书假设你已对 Kubernetes 有基本了解。它不是 Kubernetes 入门书，需要你熟悉其概念与特性。若需要更全面的基础，推荐 Marko Lukša 的《Kubernetes in Action》（Manning, 2018），或 Bilgin Ibryam 与 Roland Huß 的《Kubernetes Patterns》（O’Reilly, 2023），深入学习 Kubernetes 原理与最佳实践。

The insights shared in this book explore and dive into the exploding landscape of productization of generative AI on Kubernetes. We are on the same journey, presenting and demonstrating emerging principles and patterns.

本书分享的洞见探索并深入剖析生成式 AI 在 Kubernetes 上产品化这一蓬勃发展的领域。我们与你同行，展示并演示正在涌现的原则与模式。

What You Will Learn
你将学到什么

In this book, you will explore how to leverage Kubernetes to operationalize generative AI models, addressing the unique challenges and solutions required to run LLMs effectively on this platform. We will demonstrate why Kubernetes is an excellent choice for running complex applications that integrate AI models and usual business logic, ensuring a seamless, efficient, and scalable deployment process.

本书中你将探索如何利用 Kubernetes 运营生成式 AI 模型，应对在该平台上高效运行 LLM 所需的独特挑战与解决方案。我们会展示为什么 Kubernetes 是运行整合了 AI 模型与常规业务逻辑的复杂应用的绝佳选择，确保部署流程无缝、高效、可扩展。

You’ll gain insights into the best practices, tools, and techniques needed to optimize your generative AI models in production. We’ll provide a snapshot of the tool landscape as it stands in 2026. While the ecosystem remains dynamic, you can expect insights into enduring players like Ray, Kubeflow, and vLLM, which are likely to survive the initial gold rush of generative AI tools. This perspective will help you navigate and choose the right tools for your needs.

你将获得在生产中优化生成式 AI 模型所需的最佳实践、工具与技术洞见。我们会给出 2026 年工具格局的快照。生态虽仍在快速变化，但你可以期待对 Ray、Kubeflow、vLLM 等长期玩家的洞见——它们很可能挺过生成式 AI 工具最初的淘金热。这一视角将帮你在工具迷宫中做出适合自己的选择。

Furthermore, you’ll learn how Kubernetes plays a pivotal role in scaling, resource management, and orchestration for AI workloads. By the end of this book, you will have a comprehensive understanding of how to overcome the operational hurdles of deploying LLMs on Kubernetes and how to manage and deploy AI applications efficiently.

此外，你将了解 Kubernetes 在 AI 工作负载的扩缩容、资源管理与编排中扮演的关键角色。读完本书，你将全面理解如何克服在 Kubernetes 上部署 LLM 的运维障碍，以及如何高效管理与部署 AI 应用。

The chapters focus on practical use cases, lessons learned, and best practices, aiming to equip you with the knowledge and tools to confidently transition from development to production. With plenty of examples and detailed explanations, you’ll gain hands-on experience in setting up and maintaining a robust infrastructure for your AI projects.

各章聚焦实用用例、经验教训与最佳实践，旨在让你具备从开发走向生产的知识与工具。通过大量示例与详细讲解，你将获得为 AI 项目搭建并维护稳健基础设施的动手经验。

Introduction
导言

The release of ChatGPT in 2022 was a watershed moment for the IT world. Overnight, it seemed like everything changed, not because of entirely new concepts, but due to the exponential growth in model parameters and the massive expansion of training datasets. Model parameters—the weights and biases learned during training—are often used to measure a model’s complexity and capability. But architectural innovations and training quality are just as important to how well a model actually performs. This combination of scaling parameters and expanding data pushed AI into new territory, with capabilities that were previously unimaginable.

2022 年 ChatGPT 的发布是 IT 世界的分水岭。一夜之间，一切仿佛都变了——并非因为全新的概念，而是模型参数的指数级增长与训练数据集的大规模扩张。模型参数（训练中学到的权重与偏置）常被用来衡量模型的复杂度与能力，但架构创新与训练质量对模型实际表现同样重要。参数扩张与数据扩充的合力把 AI 推入新境地，带来了此前难以想象的能力。

In the world of physics, phase transitions describe moments when small, gradual changes suddenly lead to dramatic shifts in behavior—like water turning to ice. The rise of large language models (LLMs) follows this same pattern. Since the Transformer architecture was introduced in 2017, AI had been steadily evolving, but the leap in model size, compute power, and training data scale pushed it beyond a tipping point. These models began exhibiting human-like text generation and processing, disrupting entire industries and resetting our expectations of what AI can do. The graph in Figure I-1 shows the growth of these parameters and the expanding data sources that have enabled AI’s evolution over the past few years.

在物理学中，相变描述的是微小渐进变化突然导致行为剧变的时刻——比如水结成冰。大语言模型（LLM）的崛起遵循同样的模式。自 2017 年 Transformer 架构提出以来，AI 一直在稳步演进，但模型规模、算力与训练数据量级的飞跃把它推过了临界点。这些模型开始展现类人的文本生成与处理能力，颠覆了整个行业，重塑了我们对 AI 能做什么的预期。图 I-1 展示了这些参数的增长以及支撑 AI 近年演进的数据源扩张。

Beyond just data, we owe this transformation to advancements in computational power, particularly the widespread adoption of GPUs for general-purpose computing through frameworks like CUDA, which enabled massive parallel processing for AI workloads. This combination of vastly more data—essentially the entire internet made available for training—and faster compute created the perfect storm, enabling rapid advancements in generative AI models.

除了数据，这一转变还要归功于算力的进步，特别是通过 CUDA 等框架把 GPU 广泛用于通用计算，从而为 AI 工作负载提供大规模并行处理能力。海量数据（几乎把整个互联网都用于训练）与更快算力的结合形成了完美风暴，推动生成式 AI 模型快速进步。

原书第 23 页

And with these advancements came new challenges, especially in managing the infrastructure required to handle such massive workloads. For example, as OpenAI detailed in its report on scaling Kubernetes to 7,500 nodes, Kubernetes emerged as a critical tool for orchestrating the immense computational needs of models like GPT-3. Its ability to autoscale clusters, dynamically adjust infrastructure, and control costs made it an essential part of deploying these large models efficiently.

伴随这些进步而来的是新挑战，尤其是管理承载如此巨大工作负载所需的基础设施。例如，正如 OpenAI 在把 Kubernetes 扩展到 7500 节点的报告中详述的，Kubernetes 已成为编排 GPT-3 这类模型巨大计算需求的关键工具。它自动扩缩集群、动态调整基础设施、控制成本的能力，使其成为高效部署这些大模型不可或缺的一环。

Most of us don’t deal with clusters at the scale of OpenAI, but the underlying principles they developed are relevant for any Kubernetes environment, whether you’re running LLMs on a small cluster or at “web scale.”

我们多数人面对的集群规模远不及 OpenAI，但他们总结出的底层原则对任何 Kubernetes 环境都适用——无论你是在小集群上跑 LLM，还是在“Web 规模”下运行。

As Kubernetes experts working on Red Hat OpenShift AI, we (the authors) were used to supporting traditional workloads—web applications, API services, and databases—but running LLMs? That was a whole new ballgame. Our first experience with these computational monsters was both exciting and overwhelming. These models were like “translucent” black boxes: we knew they were huge, needed GPUs and persistent volume space, and required health checks, but beyond that, the inner workings were opaque.

作为在 Red Hat OpenShift AI 上工作的 Kubernetes 专家，我们（作者）早已习惯支持传统工作负载——Web 应用、API 服务和数据库——但跑 LLM？那完全是另一回事。第一次面对这些“计算巨兽”既兴奋又不知所措。这些模型像“半透明”的黑盒：我们知道它们巨大、需要 GPU 和持久卷空间、需要健康检查，但除此之外，内部机理是不透明的。

We still remember our first attempt vividly. It was a disaster. The models took ages to initialize, enabling GPU usage felt like falling down a rabbit hole, and CrashLoopBackOff errors kept happening. The response times were embarrassingly slow. It became clear that we had to rethink how Kubernetes was handling these workloads.

我们仍清晰记得第一次尝试。那是一场灾难。模型初始化耗时极长，启用 GPU 像掉进兔子洞，CrashLoopBackOff 错误不断。响应时间慢得令人尴尬。我们清楚地意识到必须重新思考 Kubernetes 该如何处理这些工作负载。

原书第 24 页

After some trial and error, we managed to get things running. We fine-tuned our resource requests, optimized persistent volumes, and introduced smarter scheduling strategies to maximize GPU efficiency. Finally, the models started to work. It was a steep learning curve, but it highlighted the gap between Kubernetes’ traditional strengths and the emerging needs of AI workloads.

经过一番试错，我们终于让事情跑了起来。我们微调了资源请求、优化了持久卷、引入更智能的调度策略以最大化 GPU 效率。模型终于开始工作。学习曲线很陡，但它凸显了 Kubernetes 传统优势与 AI 工作负载新需求之间的差距。

Not everyone will face these exact same challenges, but the lessons we learned are applicable to any Kubernetes environment. As the Kubernetes community continues to close the remaining gaps to make AI workloads, especially LLMs, first-class citizens, we invite you to join us on this journey. In this book, we’ll explore the state of the art for running LLMs on Kubernetes and show you how to overcome the operational challenges that come with it.

并非每个人都会遇到完全相同的挑战，但我们学到的经验适用于任何 Kubernetes 环境。随着 Kubernetes 社区持续补齐差距、让 AI 工作负载（尤其是 LLM）成为一等公民，我们邀请你加入这段旅程。本书将探索在 Kubernetes 上运行 LLM 的最新实践，并展示如何克服随之而来的运维挑战。

In this introduction, we will first explore the challenges of running large AI workloads at scale, then discuss how Kubernetes addresses them. We’ll then provide an optional primer on LLM fundamentals, covering concepts like token processing and inference phases that help when diagnosing performance issues. You can skip this section on a first read if you prefer to treat LLMs as pure black boxes. Finally, we’ll provide an overview of the four parts that guide the rest of this book: inference, production readiness, tuning, and AI-driven applications. Now, let’s dive into the first critical topic: the challenges of running generative AI at scale.

在本导言中，我们先探讨大规模运行大型 AI 工作负载的挑战，再讨论 Kubernetes 如何应对。随后给出一节可选的 LLM 基础入门，涵盖 token 处理与推理阶段等概念，有助于诊断性能问题。如果你更愿意把 LLM 当纯黑盒，初读时可跳过这节。最后概述引导本书其余部分的四个板块：推理、生产就绪、调优与 AI 驱动应用。现在，让我们深入第一个关键主题：大规模运行生成式 AI 的挑战。

Challenges of Running Generative AI at Scale
大规模运行生成式 AI 的挑战

As we have seen, running generative AI models, particularly LLMs, involves addressing a set of complex challenges that go beyond traditional application workloads. These challenges demand not just powerful hardware but also sophisticated management and orchestration of resources.

如前所述，运行生成式 AI 模型（尤其是 LLM）需要应对一系列超越传统应用工作负载的复杂挑战。这些挑战不仅需要强大的硬件，还需要对资源进行精细的管理与编排。

Sidebar: Generative AI and LLMs

In this book, we frequently use the terms “generative AI” and “LLMs” interchangeably. Here’s why:

本书中我们经常把“生成式 AI”与“LLM”交替使用。原因如下：

Generative AI encompasses a wide range of machine learning techniques that generate new content. This includes not only LLMs but also models for generating images, videos, and sound.

生成式 AI 涵盖一大类生成新内容的机器学习技术，不仅包括 LLM，还包括生成图像、视频和声音的模型。

While LLMs are just one subset of generative AI, they have become the most prominent and widely recognized. To simplify our discussion, we’ll often refer to both generative AI and LLMs interchangeably.

LLM 只是生成式 AI 的一个子集，却已成为最显眼、最广为人知的一类。为简化讨论，我们常把生成式 AI 与 LLM 交替使用。

Operationally, all generative AI models share many similarities, though we will highlight any differences when necessary.

从运维角度看，所有生成式 AI 模型有许多共性；必要时我们会指出差异。

原书第 25 页

While most of the inner working of such models can be hidden for the operator, there are still requirements that make AI workloads special:

尽管这些模型的大部分内部机理对运维者可以隐藏，但仍有一些需求让 AI 工作负载显得特殊：

Model size and resource demands
模型规模与资源需求

One of the most significant challenges in running LLMs at scale is their size. LLMs consist of billions of parameters, making them resource-intensive in terms of both storage and memory. As these models grow in complexity and size, the need for efficient resource management becomes essential. The infrastructure must be capable of handling the demands of these models without compromising performance or reliability. This is where the ability to dynamically allocate resources based on load and demand becomes crucial.

大规模运行 LLM 最大的挑战之一就是其规模。LLM 由数十亿参数构成，在存储与内存两方面都极为消耗资源。随着模型复杂度与规模增长，高效资源管理变得至关重要。基础设施必须能承受这些模型的需求而不牺牲性能或可靠性。此时，根据负载与需求动态分配资源的能力就显得极为关键。

Start-up time and latency
启动时间与延迟

LLMs face latency challenges at two critical stages. First, start-up time can be a significant bottleneck: unlike traditional applications, serving LLMs requires substantial warm-up periods where parameters are loaded into memory and optimized for inference. Second, request latency during inference can be high, as generating responses token by token takes considerable time compared to traditional request-response patterns. Both factors impact the overall responsiveness of AI-driven applications, requiring not only efficient orchestration but also request optimizations with aggressive semantic caching and routing.

LLM 在两个关键阶段面临延迟挑战。首先，启动时间可能是重大瓶颈：与传统应用不同，服务 LLM 需要大量预热时间，把参数加载进内存并为推理做优化。其次，推理期间的请求延迟可能很高——逐 token 生成回复相比传统请求-响应模式要花多得多的时间。这两个因素都影响 AI 驱动应用的整体响应性，不仅需要高效编排，还需要激进的语义缓存与路由等请求优化。

Hardware requirements and scalability
硬件需求与可扩展性

Generative AI workloads are highly dependent on specialized hardware, particularly GPUs, which provide the necessary computational power for inference and fine-tuning. Ensuring the right allocation of GPUs, managing their availability, and scaling services across multiple nodes is a challenge that requires advanced orchestration tools. Additionally, as you adopt different models with varying hardware needs, the infrastructure must accommodate new GPU types and configurations without disrupting existing workloads.

生成式 AI 工作负载高度依赖专用硬件，尤其是 GPU——它为推理与微调提供所需算力。确保 GPU 的合理分配、管理其可用性、跨多节点扩展服务，是需要高级编排工具才能应对的挑战。此外，当你采用硬件需求各异的不同模型时，基础设施必须在不影响现有工作负载的前提下容纳新的 GPU 类型与配置。

Security and data privacy
安全与数据隐私

Security is another critical concern. LLMs are often trained on sensitive data, requiring stringent security measures to protect against unauthorized access and ensure compliance with data privacy regulations. The challenge is to implement security at multiple layers, from securing the data pipeline to ensuring that the models themselves are not vulnerable to attacks.

安全是另一个关键问题。LLM 常基于敏感数据训练，需要严格的安全措施以防未授权访问并确保符合数据隐私法规。挑战在于在多层实施安全：从保护数据流水线，到确保模型自身不被攻击。

The next section examines how Kubernetes capabilities map to these AI workload requirements.

下一节考察 Kubernetes 的能力如何对应这些 AI 工作负载需求。

原书第 26 页

Kubernetes for AI Workloads
面向 AI 工作负载的 Kubernetes

Kubernetes is an open source container orchestration platform originally developed by Google, now part of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF). It was designed to automate the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications, which are packaged as OCI-compliant container images. Kubernetes abstracts the underlying infrastructure, allowing developers and operators to focus on deploying and managing applications without worrying about the complexities of the underlying hardware.

Kubernetes 是一个开源容器编排平台，最初由 Google 开发，现隶属云原生计算基金会（CNCF）。它旨在自动化容器化应用的部署、扩缩容与管理，这些应用被打包为符合 OCI 标准的容器镜像。Kubernetes 抽象了底层基础设施，让开发者与运维者专注于部署和管理应用，而不必操心底层硬件的复杂性。

Initially, Kubernetes was optimized for distributed stateless workloads that can scale horizontally with ease. However, Kubernetes quickly learned how to support stateful workloads, like databases and messaging systems. This evolution made Kubernetes a good platform for running a full stack of applications, from simple web services to complex, state-dependent systems.

最初，Kubernetes 为可轻松水平扩展的分布式无状态工作负载做了优化。但它很快学会了支持有状态工作负载，如数据库与消息系统。这一演进让 Kubernetes 成为运行全栈应用的良好平台——从简单 Web 服务到复杂的状态相关系统。

In the context of AI, Kubernetes presents both opportunities and challenges. AI workloads have unique infrastructure requirements that differ significantly from typical business applications. This is especially true for workloads involving LLMs or other generative AI models. These workloads often demand high-performance computing resources and specialized hardware, such as GPUs. The challenge lies in extending Kubernetes to handle these demands effectively while maintaining its strengths in managing business applications.

在 AI 语境下，Kubernetes 机遇与挑战并存。AI 工作负载有独特的基础设施需求，与典型业务应用差异显著，涉及 LLM 或其他生成式 AI 模型时尤其如此。这些工作负载常需要高性能计算资源与 GPU 等专用硬件。挑战在于扩展 Kubernetes 以有效应对这些需求，同时保持它在管理业务应用上的优势。

This book explores how to use Kubernetes to operationalize generative AI models. We address the specific challenges of running these workloads on a platform originally designed for traditional applications. While we assume some Kubernetes skills, we will delve into how Kubernetes’ features can be used to support AI workloads and how additional Kubernetes add-ons and platforms like Kubeflow can help fill the gaps, particularly in areas like inference and model customization.

本书探索如何用 Kubernetes 运营生成式 AI 模型。我们讨论在一个最初为传统应用设计的平台上运行这些工作负载的具体挑战。虽然假设你已具备一定 Kubernetes 技能，我们仍会深入讲解如何用 Kubernetes 的特性支持 AI 工作负载，以及 Kubeflow 等附加组件与平台如何帮助填补空白，尤其是在推理与模型定制领域。

Before diving into the rest of the book, it’s helpful to understand some LLM fundamentals. The next section provides an optional primer on these concepts.

在进入本书其余内容之前，了解一些 LLM 基础会有帮助。下一节提供这些概念的可选入门。

原书第 27 页

Understanding LLM Fundamentals
理解 LLM 基础

Throughout this book, we treat LLMs as operational “dark-gray boxes.” We manage their infrastructure, resources, and lifecycle without diving deep into neural network architectures or training mathematics. This approach is sufficient for most operational tasks.

贯穿本书，我们把 LLM 当作运维上的“深灰盒”。我们管理其基础设施、资源与生命周期，而不深入神经网络架构或训练数学。这种方式对大多数运维任务已足够。

However, understanding some LLM fundamentals helps when you encounter specialized concepts like Time To First Token (TTFT), token throughput, or key-value (KV) cache management. These operational metrics are rooted in how LLMs actually process text. A basic understanding makes it easier to diagnose performance issues or optimize resources.

然而，理解一些 LLM 基础，能让你在遇到首 token 时延（TTFT）、token 吞吐、键值（KV）缓存管理等专业概念时更从容。这些运维指标根植于 LLM 实际处理文本的方式。有了基本理解，诊断性能问题或优化资源都会更容易。

提示：本节为可选内容。如果你更愿意把 LLM 当作纯黑盒，可直接跳到“Overview”（第 xxxiii 页），等后续讲到 LLM 内部（如第 5 章的指标）时再回来。

Think of this section as a primer that bridges the gap between complete opacity and unnecessary detail. We’ll cover just enough to make operational decisions informed by how LLMs work, not how to build one.

可以把本节看作衔接“完全不透明”与“不必要细节”之间的入门。我们只讲够用的部分，让你基于 LLM 的工作原理做运维决策，而不是教你如何造一个 LLM。

How LLMs Process Text
LLM 如何处理文本

As mentioned in “Generative AI and LLMs” on page xxiii, LLMs are a subset of the models under the generative AI category. They are based on the Transformer architecture and are used to process text (natural language) to perform a number of different tasks. An example of a task is to produce a summary of a longer text, or to ask the model to answer user questions or classify some data. Modern LLMs increasingly support multimodal inputs, where images, audio, or video are encoded alongside text for processing. The Transformer architecture describes an encoding phase and a decoding phase. This has been used to create three different classes of models: encoder only models, encoder-decoder models, and decoder-only models.

正如第 xxiii 页“生成式 AI 与 LLM”一节所说，LLM 是生成式 AI 大类下的一个子集。它们基于 Transformer 架构，用于处理文本（自然语言）以完成各种任务。任务示例包括：为较长文本生成摘要、让模型回答用户问题、或对某些数据分类。现代 LLM 越来越多地支持多模态输入——图像、音频或视频与文本一起编码后处理。Transformer 架构描述了编码阶段与解码阶段，据此产生了三类模型：仅编码器模型、编码器-解码器模型，以及仅解码器模型。

In general, encoder models are popular for learning embeddings used in classification tasks. Examples include Google BERT and Meta RoBERTa. Encoder-decoder models were originally designed for generative tasks like translation or summarization, where input and output are strongly connected. Google Flan-T5 is a well-known example. Decoder-only models are used for generative tasks, particularly conversational AI and text generation. The OpenAI GPT series (GPT-1, GPT-2, and GPT-3) follows this architecture.

一般来说，编码器模型常用于学习分类任务所用的嵌入，例如 Google BERT 与 Meta RoBERTa。编码器-解码器模型最初为翻译、摘要等生成式任务设计，这些任务中输入与输出强相关，Google Flan-T5 是知名例子。仅解码器模型用于生成式任务，尤其是对话式 AI 与文本生成。OpenAI GPT 系列（GPT-1、GPT-2、GPT-3）即采用此架构。

In practice, today the majority of models adopted for text generation are decoder-only. Modern decoder-only models can also perform translation and summarization tasks effectively, even without the dedicated encoder step that was originally considered necessary for these tasks. We will focus on decoder-only models, but LLMs can also serve encoder-decoder models, and the inference pipeline described here is analogous.

实践中，如今用于文本生成的模型多数是仅解码器的。现代仅解码器模型即使没有原来认为这些任务所必需的专用编码步骤，也能有效完成翻译与摘要。我们将聚焦仅解码器模型，但 LLM 同样可以服务编码器-解码器模型，此处描述的推理流水线类似。

Tokenization and Embeddings
分词与嵌入

From a practical perspective, an LLM is a complex neural network that processes and generates numbers rather than text. Therefore it requires a conversion layer to make it more usable. A naive way to perform this conversion is to create a huge vocabulary of all possible words and use the index of this vocabulary as an integer representation of a word. With this approach, every time a word does not exist in the vocabulary, the conversation cannot happen and the word is classified as unknown.

从实用角度看，LLM 是一个复杂神经网络，它处理并生成数字而非文本，因此需要一个转换层使其更可用。一种朴素做法是建一个包含所有可能单词的巨大词表，用词表索引作为某个词的整数表示。这样一来，每当出现词表中没有的词，对话就无法进行，该词被归类为未知。

Modern LLMs use subword tokenization, where text is broken into smaller units, called tokens, of various sizes rather than whole words. For example, the word “regularization” might be split into “regular” and “ization” as separate tokens. This approach allows the model to handle any text input, including rare words, technical terms, or names like “O’Reilly,” by combining subword units from a fixed vocabulary of tens of thousands of tokens. Unlike word-level approaches, subword tokenization eliminates the unknown word problem while keeping vocabulary sizes manageable (see the following sidebar for more on prompts and tokens).

现代 LLM 使用子词分词：把文本切成大小不一、称为 token 的更小单元，而非整个单词。例如 “regularization” 可能被切成 “regular” 和 “ization” 两个 token。这种方式让模型能处理任意文本输入——包括生僻词、技术术语或像 “O’Reilly” 这样的名字——通过从一个数万 token 的固定词表中组合子词单元。与词级方法不同，子词分词消除了未登录词问题，同时词表规模可控（关于 prompt 与 token 见下面侧栏）。

Fortunately, converting a sentence into words and then into numbers is not a challenge unique to LLMs but is common to all NLP techniques. Years of research in this field have led to the development of various approaches.

幸运的是，把句子转成词再转成数字并非 LLM 独有的挑战，而是所有 NLP 技术共有的。该领域多年研究已发展出多种方法。

The solution that LLMs use is based on the adoption of a tokenizer that splits the sentence in tokens and then computes the token embedding to capture the semantic meaning with a numerical representation. This is a necessary preparation to make the input consumable by the neural network.

LLM 采用的方案是：用一个 tokenizer 把句子切分成 token，再计算 token 嵌入，以数值表示捕捉语义。这是让输入可被神经网络消费所必需的准备步骤。

原书第 28 页

Sidebar: Prompt, Sentence, Word, and Token

The prompt is the request that is sent to the LLM to be processed. It can be a simple question or a very long text with a lot of contextual information to process. In a real-world scenario, the prompt is not limited to the actual end user input but also includes at least a system prompt that guides the LLM behavior. The system prompt is included in the full request and defines the scenario that the model should use to handle the user request.

prompt 是发送给 LLM 待处理的请求。它可以是一个简单问题，也可以是包含大量上下文信息的超长文本。在真实场景中，prompt 不限于最终用户的实际输入，至少还包含一个引导 LLM 行为的系统 prompt。系统 prompt 包含在完整请求中，定义模型处理用户请求时应采用的场景。

A system prompt can strongly influence the model’s behavior. For an AI assistant, the system prompt might be: “You are a friendly AI assistant named John. Your role is to help users with easy to understand answers. If you don’t know the answer, just say that you don’t know instead of guessing.” The same model can perform text summarization with a system prompt like: “Please generate a summary of the following text highlighting main points in no more than 500 words.”

系统 prompt 能强烈影响模型行为。对一个 AI 助手，系统 prompt 可能是：“你是一个友好的 AI 助手，名叫 John。你的职责是用通俗易懂的答案帮助用户。如果不知道答案，就直说不知道，不要瞎猜。” 同一个模型配上类似“请为以下文本生成不超过 500 字、突出要点的摘要”的系统 prompt，就能做文本摘要。

Altering the prompt to include more context and influence the generation of the output is called prompt engineering.

通过修改 prompt 加入更多上下文、影响输出生成，称为 prompt 工程。

The prompt is formed by one or more sentences. The sentence structure is preserved during the tokenization using special tokens to identify the beginning, the end, and the punctuation. In natural language, the structure of the sentence influences the semantics; thus it is critical to preserve it during the tokenization and avoid a flat list of tokens.

prompt 由一个或多个句子构成。分词时用特殊 token 标记句首、句尾与标点，以保留句子结构。在自然语言中，句子结构影响语义，因此分词时保留结构、避免变成一串扁平 token 至关重要。

Each element of the sentence is a word that maps to one or more token. This is because we want to keep the size of the vocabulary fixed so we cannot map every possible combination of letters that are rarely used or even never used at all. Splitting a word in tokens is way more efficient: the words tall, taller, and tallest can be split as (tall), (tall, er), and (tall, est), so that the tokens er and est can be reused for other words that have the same suffix. The tokenizer algorithm used during the training produces the vocabulary that the model recognizes. Thus, given an input sentence, there is no single way to calculate how many tokens are produced by the tokenizer. In general, a word is split in multiple tokens every time there is no direct mapping in the vocabulary. This prevents the possibility of a word being discharged because of a missing direct conversion.

句子中的每个元素是一个词，映射到一个或多个 token。这是因为我们要保持词表大小固定，无法为所有罕见甚至从未出现的字母组合都建映射。把词拆成 token 效率高得多：tall、taller、tallest 可分别拆为 (tall)、(tall, er)、(tall, est)，于是 er、est 这两个 token 可被其他同后缀词复用。训练时使用的 tokenizer 算法决定了模型识别的词表。因此，给定一句输入，无法用单一方法算出 tokenizer 会产出多少 token。一般来说，只要词表中没有直接映射，一个词就会被拆成多个 token，这避免了因缺少直接转换而把词丢弃的可能。

Some tokens are special because they don’t map to a word; instead, they represent a special meaning like end of the generated text (<EOS>) or beginning and end of the system prompt.

有些 token 是特殊的，它们不对应某个词，而是表示特殊含义，例如生成文本结束（<EOS>），或系统 prompt 的起止。

原书第 29 页

Tokenizer implementation
Tokenizer 实现

A tokenizer is an algorithm that takes a sentence as input and returns a list of tokens as output. A token is usually a subword and it is language-specific: for example, er is a common suffix in English, so it is a token. Each token has an integer representation (i.e., the index of the vocabulary), so it is possible to convert the full sentence in a sequence of numbers where each number represents a token. Because each number represents a single token, it is also possible to convert a number back to the original token.

tokenizer 是一个算法，输入句子、输出 token 列表。token 通常是子词，且与语言相关：例如 er 是英语常见后缀，所以是一个 token。每个 token 有一个整数表示（即词表中的索引），因此可以把整句转换成一串数字，每个数字代表一个 token。由于每个数字代表单个 token，也可以把数字反查回原始 token。

State-of-the-art tokenizer implementations are far more complex than this simple description. They incorporate normalization steps, model-specific token handling, techniques for languages without space-separated words, concurrent implementations, and much more. Different tokenizers are available and one of the most commonly used is the Hugging Face tokenizer library. The same tokenizer used during model training must be used during inference to ensure consistent token mappings. The tokenizer vocabulary itself is fixed; it’s the embedding layer (covered next) that’s trained during model development.

最先进的 tokenizer 实现远比这段简单描述复杂。它们包含归一化步骤、模型专属的 token 处理、针对无空格分词语言的技术、并发实现等等。可用的 tokenizer 有很多种，最常用之一是 Hugging Face tokenizer 库。推理时必须使用与训练时相同的 tokenizer，以保证 token 映射一致。tokenizer 词表本身是固定的；在模型开发过程中训练的是嵌入层（下一节讲）。

For a more comprehensive introduction to the tokenizer topic, see the “Summary of the tokenizer” page on the Hugging Face website.

要更全面了解 tokenizer，参见 Hugging Face 网站上的“Summary of the tokenizer”页面。

原书第 30 页

Embeddings
嵌入

Now that we have converted the input of the user to a list of tokens, we are ready for the second step: the embedding.

既然已把用户输入转换成 token 列表，就可以进行第二步：嵌入。

Thanks to the tokenizer we now have a vector of numbers that represents the original input, but it doesn’t have any information on the semantic meaning of the token. We cannot use this number to compare tokens because it just represents the index of the position of the token in the vocabulary.

有了 tokenizer，我们现在有了一个代表原始输入的数字向量，但它不含 token 的语义信息。我们不能用这个数字来比较 token，因为它只代表 token 在词表中的位置索引。

Embedding is a process that generates a vector representation of the input, capturing its semantic meaning. This means that the distance between two embedding vectors is smaller if they represent semantically similar inputs, and larger if the inputs are not strongly related.

嵌入是为输入生成向量表示、捕捉其语义的过程。这意味着：若两个输入语义相近，它们嵌入向量间的距离就较小；若输入关联不强，距离就较大。

In other words, consider this example: the tokens dog and puppy are related to each other, so their embedding representations produce vectors with a smaller distance compared to the embeddings for dog and car.

换句话说：token dog 与 puppy 彼此相关，所以它们的嵌入向量之间的距离，要比 dog 与 car 的嵌入距离更小。

Similar to the tokenizer, the model’s embedding layer is learned during training. At this stage, the token vocabulary is fixed, and each token ID is associated with a learned vector in an embedding matrix. These token embeddings capture a token’s typical semantic relationships to other tokens in a high-dimensional space. Later, as the model processes an input sequence, these static token embeddings are transformed into contextual representations that depend on the surrounding tokens. See Figure I-2 for a simplified visual example of embeddings. If you want to learn more on the topic, we suggest “The Illustrated Word2vec” blogpost.

与 tokenizer 类似，模型的嵌入层是在训练中学到的。此时 token 词表固定，每个 token ID 关联到嵌入矩阵中一个学到的向量。这些 token 嵌入在高维空间中捕捉一个 token 与其他 token 的典型语义关系。随后，当模型处理输入序列时，这些静态 token 嵌入会被转换为依赖上下文 token 的表示。嵌入的简化可视化例子见图 I-2。想深入了解，推荐“The Illustrated Word2vec”博文。

The embedding techniques described here are specific to text embeddings. However, it is also possible to convert image, video, or audio data and make it available to the model as part of a multimodal vocabulary. This is necessary when working with a multimodal model that supports additional input modalities, such as images or video, alongside text.

这里描述的嵌入技术针对文本嵌入。但图像、视频或音频数据也可以被转换，作为多模态词表的一部分提供给模型。当你使用除文本外还支持图像或视频等输入模态的多模态模型时，这是必要的。

原书第 31 页

注意：多数托管 LLM 服务（如 OpenAI ChatGPT）采用按 token 计费。你可以固定价格购买一定数量的 token（通常为一百万）。既然我们已弄清词与 token 的区别，就能更好理解为什么这些服务用 token 而非词计费：token 是 LLM 的处理单元，而词不是。这有个副作用：终端用户更难预估一次请求的成本。经验法则是英文约 4 个字符算 1 个 token，但这只是平均估计。tokenizer 因模型而异，同一输入在不同模型下可能被切成不同数量的 token。此外，输入与输出 token 都计入请求总成本，因此无法事先预估成本——我们无法预测模型会生成多少 token，只能用参数设定生成 token 的上限。

The Two Phases of Inference
推理的两个阶段

From a high-level perspective, the end-to-end inference pipeline has two steps: prefill and decode. The prefill phase tokenizes the input, applies embedding, and generates the first token. After that, the decode phase generates the tokens one by one and computes the output text (Figure I-3).

从高层看，端到端推理流水线有两步：prefill（预填充）与 decode（解码）。prefill 阶段对输入分词、做嵌入，并生成第一个 token。之后 decode 阶段逐个生成 token 并拼出输出文本（图 I-3）。

The two phases use the model in the same way to produce a token, but while the prefill input processing is done in parallel, the decoding phase produces one token at a time. This makes the prefill workload compute-bound, while the decode phase is memory-bound.

两个阶段用模型生成 token 的方式相同，但 prefill 的输入处理是并行的，而 decode 阶段一次只产出一个 token。这使得 prefill 工作负载是计算密集型（compute-bound），而 decode 阶段是内存密集型（memory-bound）。

The compute-bound and memory-bound terms refer to the computational complexity of a particular program or algorithm. An algorithm is compute-bound when the time to complete the task is driven mainly by the speed of the processing unit (CPU or GPU in this case). It is memory-bound when the amount of free memory and the speed to access (aka bandwidth) memory are the primary factors that drive the completion time. This implies that you need a faster processing unit to speed up a compute-bound problem, while you need more or faster memory in the case of a memory-bound scenario. Figure I-4 represents resource utilization in the two different cases.

compute-bound 与 memory-bound 这两个术语指特定程序或算法的计算复杂度。当完成任务的时间主要由处理单元（这里是 CPU 或 GPU）速度决定时，称该算法是计算密集的；当可用内存大小与内存访问速度（即带宽）是决定完成时间的主要因素时，则是内存密集的。这意味着：要加速计算密集问题，需要更快的处理单元；而内存密集场景则需要更大或更快的内存。图 I-4 展示了两种情况下的资源利用。

原书第 32 页

As shown in Figure I-4, compute-bound workloads max out processing capacity, while memory-bound workloads are limited by memory bandwidth. Now let’s dive into the prefill and decode phases in more detail.

如图 I-4 所示，计算密集型工作负载会占满处理能力，而内存密集型工作负载受限于内存带宽。下面更详细地看 prefill 与 decode 两个阶段。

Prefill

The prefill phase works as an initialization phase where the input prompt is processed and the first token is produced. The first step to load the prompt is to convert the text to numbers using tokenizer and embedding.

prefill 阶段充当初始化阶段：处理输入 prompt 并生成第一个 token。加载 prompt 的第一步是用 tokenizer 与嵌入把文本转成数字。

The last step of the prefill is the execution of the model (aka forward pass) to generate the first token.

prefill 的最后一步是执行模型（即前向传播）以生成第一个 token。

The prefill phase has two operational characteristics worth noting: it is compute-bound and the tokenizer runs entirely on CPU. Modern CPUs and GPUs are very fast, and tokenizer implementation is highly optimized, so the prefill is rarely a throughput bottleneck—but it does directly affect time to first token. Some models are now able to handle inputs of about one million tokens. For reference, the complete Lord of the Rings trilogy contains about half a million words (approximately 600,000 tokens).

prefill 阶段有两个运维上值得注意的特点：它是计算密集的，且 tokenizer 完全在 CPU 上运行。现代 CPU 与 GPU 都很快，tokenizer 实现也高度优化，所以 prefill 很少成为吞吐瓶颈——但它直接影响首 token 时延。现在有些模型能处理约一百万 token 的输入。作为参照，整部《魔戒》三部曲约有 50 万词（约 60 万 token）。

原书第 33 页

Decode

After the prefill, the user’s prompt is parsed, loaded, and the first token is produced with a single forward pass of the neural network. The decode phase is in charge of the generation of the rest of the tokens until the end-of-stream token (<EOS>) is produced or the max number of tokens to be generated is reached. This phase cannot be parallelized and it has to proceed one token at a time because of the autoregressive nature of the generation. Autoregressive means that each generated token is based on the previous sequence and becomes part of the previous state used to generate the next one. At each iteration, the entire sequence (input prompt + generated tokens) is used to produce the next token. There is an attention vector for each token of the sequence so the consequence of this iterative process is that the attention vector has a cost that scales quadratically with the total sequence length.

prefill 之后，用户 prompt 被解析、加载，并经神经网络一次前向传播生成第一个 token。decode 阶段负责生成其余 token，直到产出流结束 token（<EOS>）或达到最大生成 token 数。由于生成的自回归特性，这一阶段无法并行，必须逐 token 进行。自回归意味着每个生成的 token 都基于前一序列，并成为用于生成下一个 token 的先前状态的一部分。每次迭代都用整个序列（输入 prompt + 已生成 token）来产出下一个 token。序列中每个 token 都有一个注意力向量，因此这种迭代过程的代价是：注意力向量的开销随序列总长度平方级增长。

The optimization of this quadratic cost is the key bottleneck for the scalability of LLM inference, especially with very long generated sequences.

优化这一平方级代价是 LLM 推理可扩展性的关键瓶颈，尤其是在生成序列很长时。

There are various approaches to address this problem, each tackling it from a different angle. Some approaches are more experimental, such as using a smaller draft model to generate candidate tokens that are then verified in parallel by the larger target model (speculative decoding). Others, like KV caching to save intermediate steps and avoid recomputing them, are already standard in all runtimes.

解决这个问题有多种思路，各自从不同角度切入。有些偏实验性，比如用一个较小的草稿模型生成候选 token，再由大模型并行验证（投机解码）。另一些——如保存中间步骤、避免重算的 KV 缓存——已成为所有运行时的标准做法。

Let’s focus on KV caching. We already mentioned that the decoding phase of the generation is memory-bound. The availability and management of memory directly impacts the max throughput that the runtime can produce—but why?

让我们聚焦 KV 缓存。前面提过生成的 decode 阶段是内存密集的。内存的可用性与管理直接影响运行时能达到的最大吞吐——但为什么？

The autoregressive nature of the generation phase makes it use the entire previous sequence. This means that after every generation step, the runtime must compute the attention values for each of the previous tokens, making the generation phase highly inefficient. Most of the values have been already computed except for the last token. A KV cache is introduced to avoid this computation, where the keys are the tokens and the values are the attentions vectors. This moves the scalability challenges from the computation side to the cost of storing and accessing all the previous values, making the problem memory-bound. Optimizations like Flash Attention address this by minimizing data movement between GPU memory levels during attention computation.

生成阶段的自回归特性使其要使用整个先前序列。这意味着每步生成后，运行时都必须为每个先前 token 计算注意力值，使生成阶段极其低效。除了最后一个 token，大多数值其实已经算过。引入 KV 缓存就是为了避免这种重复计算：key 是 token，value 是注意力向量。这把可扩展性挑战从计算侧转移到存储与访问所有先前值的开销上，使问题变为内存密集。Flash Attention 等优化通过在注意力计算期间最小化 GPU 各显存层级间的数据搬移来应对这一点。

Moreover, given that we cannot predict the total length of the output, we cannot estimate the size of this cache. The original implementation of this cache required contiguous memory to store it. This limitation has now been addressed with PagedAttention, which introduces the concept of paginated memory, similar to how operating systems manage memory. It splits the cache into blocks and accesses them via a lookup table.

此外，由于无法预测输出总长度，我们无法预估这个缓存的大小。该缓存最初的实现需要连续内存来存储。如今 PagedAttention 解决了这一限制，它引入分页内存的概念，类似操作系统管理内存的方式：把缓存切成块，通过查找表访问。

原书第 34 页

The usage of this lookup table to access memory blocks enables the sharing of the same KV cache across multiple generations. Parallel sampling techniques use the same prompt to generate multiple outputs, and the cache can speed up the overall process in this case. The end goal of projects like vLLM is to maximize the throughput by serving multiple requests in parallel, with many other optimizations to achieve this (like continuous batching).

用查找表访问内存块，使得同一份 KV 缓存可在多次生成间共享。并行采样技术用同一个 prompt 生成多个输出，此时缓存可加速整个过程。vLLM 等项目的最终目标是通过并行服务多个请求来最大化吞吐，并辅以连续批处理等众多优化。

The decode phase handles the generation of all tokens and more. In reality, each pass doesn’t produce a single token but a list of candidates, followed by a projection step to select the desired result.

decode 阶段处理所有 token 的生成，还不止于此。实际上，每次前向传播并不只产出一个 token，而是一组候选，再经一个投影步骤选出所需结果。

The sampling logic to select the next token is not trivial and is influenced by some parameters like temperature, top-k, and top-p to guide the level of “randomness” of the generation. If you want to learn more, we suggest the “Sampling Methods in Text Generation Unlocking Diversity and Creativity” blogpost.

选择下一个 token 的采样逻辑并不简单，受 temperature、top-k、top-p 等参数影响，用以调节生成的“随机性”。想深入了解，推荐“Sampling Methods in Text Generation Unlocking Diversity and Creativity”博文。

The reverse embedder is the final step before returning the token to the user. It uses the same lookup table that was used to convert a token to the embedding vector to do the opposite and return the textual representation of each token.

反向嵌入器是把 token 返回给用户之前的最后一步。它用当初把 token 转成嵌入向量的那张查找表做逆操作，返回每个 token 的文本表示。

Most of the work in the decode phase happens on the GPU. However, since it is memory-bound, it may not fully utilize the GPU’s processing power, spending much of the time moving KV cache data to and from GPU memory. This is a high-level description of how the inference pipeline works. There is much more to discuss, and the field is still evolving.

decode 阶段的大部分工作在 GPU 上进行。但由于它是内存密集的，可能无法充分利用 GPU 的处理能力，很多时间花在 KV 缓存数据与 GPU 显存之间的来回搬移上。这是对推理流水线工作方式的高层描述。还有更多可讲，领域也仍在演进。

Now that we have a basic understanding of how LLMs process text and generate responses, we can better appreciate the operational challenges they present on Kubernetes. Resource allocation during prefill, memory management during decode, and token-based optimization all stem from these fundamentals. These concepts will resurface throughout the book when we discuss metrics, optimization, and scaling strategies.

既然我们已对 LLM 如何处理文本、生成回复有了基本理解，就能更好体会它们在 Kubernetes 上带来的运维挑战。prefill 期间的资源分配、decode 期间的内存管理、基于 token 的优化，都源于这些基础原理。在后续讨论指标、优化与扩缩容策略时，这些概念会反复出现。

With this foundation in place, let’s turn to the structure of the book itself.

有了这个基础，让我们转向本书本身的结构。

原书第 35 页

Overview
总览

As we discussed in “Challenges of Running Generative AI at Scale” on page xxiii, running generative AI on Kubernetes introduces a range of unique challenges that require innovative solutions. This book is organized into four parts, each addressing a critical phase of operationalizing LLMs on Kubernetes. The progression reflects how teams typically adopt AI: starting with inference, maturing toward production-grade operations, customizing models when needed, and finally building complete AI-driven applications.

正如第 xxiii 页“大规模运行生成式 AI 的挑战”所讨论的，在 Kubernetes 上运行生成式 AI 带来一系列独特挑战，需要创新的解决方案。本书分为四个部分，每个部分应对在 Kubernetes 上运营 LLM 的一个关键阶段。这一递进反映了团队通常采用 AI 的方式：从推理起步，走向生产级运维，按需定制模型，最终构建完整的 AI 驱动应用。

With the fundamentals in place and the landscape mapped, let’s dive into the details and explore what each part covers, beginning with the foundation of LLM operations on Kubernetes: inference.

有了基础、摸清了格局，让我们深入细节，看看各部分讲什么——先从 Kubernetes 上 LLM 运维的基础：推理讲起。

Inference

The most common use case for running GenAI on Kubernetes is to offer querying the model as a service. This process is known as inference. Inference involves using the trained model to generate predictions or outputs based on new inputs. To serve these models to a wide range of users, they must be deployed in a scalable and reliable manner. This is where Kubernetes shines, offering a robust platform for operationalizing inference at scale.

在 Kubernetes 上运行 GenAI 最常见的用例，就是把查询模型作为一种服务提供出去。这个过程称为推理。推理用训练好的模型基于新输入生成预测或输出。要把这些模型服务给广大用户，必须以可扩展、可靠的方式部署。Kubernetes 正擅长于此，为大规模运营推理提供了稳健平台。

Kubernetes orchestration manages GPU allocation, scheduling, and self-healing for inference workloads. Containers provide consistent execution environments, while extensions like KServe add ML-specific capabilities: autoscaling, canary rollouts, and built-in monitoring. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) enforces granular policies for managing and accessing model services.

Kubernetes 编排为推理工作负载管理 GPU 分配、调度与自愈。容器提供一致的执行环境，KServe 等扩展则加入 ML 专属能力：自动扩缩容、金丝雀发布与内建监控。基于角色的访问控制（RBAC）为管理与访问模型服务实施细粒度策略。

Part I dives deeper into these topics, exploring how to leverage Kubernetes to serve models in a production environment, ensuring they are scalable, reliable, and secure.

第一部分深入这些主题，探索如何用 Kubernetes 在生产环境中服务模型，确保其可扩展、可靠、安全。

Production Readiness

Getting a model to work once in a development environment is straightforward. Getting it to work reliably at scale, under sustained traffic, with predictable costs and behavior is an entirely different challenge. Part II addresses the operational maturity required to run LLM inference in production without surprises.

在开发环境让模型跑通一次很简单。但要让它在持续流量下可靠地大规模运行、成本与行为可预测，则完全是另一项挑战。第二部分讨论在生产中毫无意外地运行 LLM 推理所需的运维成熟度。

原书第 36 页

Once you’ve successfully deployed a model for inference, the real work begins: keeping it running efficiently under real-world conditions. Production readiness means your model can handle sustained traffic while maintaining performance, staying within budget, and surfacing the insights you need to understand what’s happening inside your deployment. Unlike traditional applications where CPU and memory metrics tell the full story, LLM workloads require specialized observability and resource management.

一旦成功部署模型用于推理，真正的工作才开始：让它在真实条件下高效运行。生产就绪意味着你的模型能在维持性能、不超预算的同时承受持续流量，并把理解部署内部状况所需的洞见呈现出来。传统应用中 CPU、内存指标就能说明一切，而 LLM 工作负载需要专门的可观测性与资源管理。

Part II examines three critical operational concerns. First, GPU management: how Kubernetes schedulers, device plug-ins, and resource limits shape throughput and utilization for expensive accelerator hardware that can cost hundreds of dollars per hour. Second, production optimization: scaling policies, rollout strategies, and failure handling that keep performance steady as demand grows, along with cost controls that prevent budget overruns. Third, observability: logs, metrics, and traces that surface LLM-specific metrics like Time To First Token, token throughput, and KV cache utilization. These metrics reveal how your model performs under load and where bottlenecks emerge.

第二部分考察三个关键运维问题。第一是 GPU 管理：Kubernetes 调度器、设备插件与资源限制如何影响每小时可能耗费数百美元的昂贵加速器硬件的吞吐与利用率。第二是生产优化：随需求增长保持性能稳定的扩缩策略、发布策略与故障处理，以及防止预算超支的成本控制。第三是可观测性：日志、指标与链路追踪，呈现 TTFT、token 吞吐、KV 缓存利用率等 LLM 专属指标。这些指标揭示模型在负载下的表现以及瓶颈出现在哪里。

We explore all of these operational challenges in depth, showing how to maintain reliability and control costs as your LLM services mature from proof-of-concept to production-grade infrastructure.

我们深入探讨所有这些运维挑战，展示在 LLM 服务从概念验证走向生产级基础设施的过程中如何保持可靠性并控制成本。

Tuning

Foundation models are powerful generalists, but they typically lack specialized knowledge in proprietary domains or specific use cases. A legal assistant needs to understand contract law terminology. A customer service bot needs to match your company’s tone and policies. A code completion tool needs to follow your organization’s coding standards. Part III covers how to customize foundation models for these specialized requirements.

基础模型是强大的通才，但通常缺乏专有领域或特定用例的专业知识。法律助手需要懂合同法术语；客服机器人需要契合公司的语气与政策；代码补全工具需要遵循组织的编码规范。第三部分讲如何为这些专门需求定制基础模型。

Rather than training models from scratch (an option available only to the largest companies with massive compute budgets), modern AI engineering focuses on tuning. Tuning refines pre-trained models through techniques like fine-tuning, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), and other parameter-efficient methods that adapt a foundation model to your specific use case.

现代 AI 工程不从头训练模型（那只有算力预算巨大的大公司才负担得起），而是聚焦于调优。调优通过微调、低秩适配（LoRA）及其他参数高效方法来精调预训练模型，使其适配你的具体用例。

The operational challenges of tuning workloads differ from inference. Tuning jobs are batch oriented, GPU intensive, and require careful resource allocation and quota management to control costs. These are not continuous services like inference endpoints, but one-off or periodic jobs that consume significant resources for hours or days. Kubernetes schedules these demanding workloads across available GPU resources and manages the lifecycle from experiment to production-ready adapter.

调优工作负载的运维挑战与推理不同。调优作业是批处理式、GPU 密集的，需要仔细的资源分配与配额管理以控制成本。它们不像推理端点那样是持续服务，而是一次性或周期性作业，会连续数小时甚至数天消耗大量资源。Kubernetes 在可用 GPU 资源上调度这些高要求工作负载，并管理从实验到生产级适配器的整个生命周期。

原书第 37 页

Part III covers both the customization techniques and the operational practices for managing tuning workloads on Kubernetes, with emphasis on job scheduling, resource optimization, and cost control.

第三部分既讲定制技术，也讲在 Kubernetes 上管理调优工作负载的运维实践，重点是作业调度、资源优化与成本控制。

AI-Driven Applications

An LLM inference service by itself is just a component. The real value emerges when you integrate it into complete applications that combine the LLM’s generation capabilities with your data, business logic, and existing systems. Part IV demonstrates how to build production-ready AI systems on Kubernetes, where the LLM is one piece in a larger microservices architecture.

LLM 推理服务本身只是一个组件。真正的价值在于把它整合进完整应用，将 LLM 的生成能力与你的数据、业务逻辑和现有系统结合。第四部分展示如何在 Kubernetes 上构建生产级 AI 系统，其中 LLM 只是更大微服务架构中的一环。

LLM inference services rarely run in isolation. Building production-ready AI systems requires understanding how to architect request flows, manage context retrieval and tool invocation, and maintain state across interactions. The key principle: keep the LLM focused on generation, while the application owns data access, side effects, and policy enforcement.

LLM 推理服务很少孤立运行。构建生产级 AI 系统需要理解如何设计请求流、管理上下文检索与工具调用、并在多次交互间维护状态。关键原则是：让 LLM 专注于生成，而应用负责数据访问、副作用与策略执行。

This part explores the architectural patterns and operational challenges of AI-driven applications. Chat-facing applications orchestrate flows between conversational backends, vector databases for context, and LLM services for generation. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds LLM outputs in external knowledge bases, combining embeddings with real-time data retrieval to provide accurate, up-to-date information. Agentic workflows take this further, enabling multistep reasoning where the LLM decides which tools to call and how to coordinate actions, but this introduces nondeterminism, variable resource consumption, and emergent failure modes like reasoning loops and cost spirals that demand specialized guardrails.

本部分探索 AI 驱动应用的架构模式与运维挑战。面向聊天的应用在对话后端、用于上下文的向量数据库与用于生成的 LLM 服务之间编排流程。检索增强生成（RAG）让 LLM 输出扎根于外部知识库，把嵌入与实时数据检索结合，提供准确、最新的信息。智能体工作流更进一步，支持多步推理——由 LLM 决定调用哪些工具、如何协调行动——但这也引入了非确定性、可变资源消耗，以及推理死循环、成本失控等涌现式失效模式，需要专门的护栏。

Operating agentic systems requires runtime controls beyond traditional microservice patterns: budget enforcement to cap token consumption, approval gates for sensitive operations, and iteration limits to prevent infinite loops. Standard protocols like the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) enable communication between agents and tools.

运营智能体系统需要传统微服务模式之外的运行时控制：限制 token 消耗的预算强制、敏感操作的审批关卡、防止死循环的迭代上限。模型上下文协议（MCP）与智能体间协议（A2A）等标准协议使智能体与工具之间能够通信。

Part IV covers both the architectural patterns and the production-hardening techniques for running AI-driven applications, with focus on security and state management.

第四部分既讲架构模式，也讲运行 AI 驱动应用的生产加固技术，重点是安全与状态管理。

With this road map in place, let’s begin our journey with Part I, where we’ll tackle the most fundamental challenge: deploying and serving models for inference on Kubernetes.

有了这张路线图，让我们从第一部分启程，应对最根本的挑战：在 Kubernetes 上部署并服务模型以做推理。

Part I: Inference
第一部分：推理

Part I discusses the key aspects to consider during the deployment and execution of a generative AI model. This is addressed first because, unlike predictive AI models, you typically don’t start from scratch by creating an entirely new foundation model. The creation of a foundation model is an extremely resource, time, and data intensive activity that adopts similar techniques but at a larger scale. A very limited number of companies perform similar activities, so it is not covered in this book.

第一部分讨论部署与执行生成式 AI 模型时要考虑的关键方面。之所以先讲它，是因为与预测式 AI 模型不同，你通常不会从零开始造一个全新的基础模型。创造基础模型是一项极其耗费资源、时间与数据的活动，采用类似技术但规模更大。只有极少数公司做这种事，因此本书不涉及。

This phase of the model lifecycle is not new to the AI space; model serving has always been a core aspect since the beginning of AI adoption in production contexts. However, the size and complexity of these new types of models introduce a significant set of new challenges. Beyond its historical importance, inference has become the primary entry point for modern AI adoption. AI engineers typically begin by integrating pre-trained models into their existing applications through inference APIs, allowing them to infuse traditional software with AI capabilities without requiring deep machine learning expertise. Moreover, inference infrastructure serves as the foundational layer for agentic AI systems, where multiple models and tools must work together seamlessly to accomplish complex tasks.

模型生命周期的这一阶段对 AI 领域并不新鲜；自 AI 进入生产场景以来，模型服务一直是核心环节。然而这类新模型的规模与复杂性带来了一整套新挑战。除了历史重要性，推理已成为现代采用 AI 的主要入口。AI 工程师通常先通过推理 API 把预训练模型集成进现有应用，让传统软件在不要求深厚 ML 专业的情况下获得 AI 能力。此外，推理基础设施还是智能体 AI 系统的基础层——在那里多个模型与工具必须无缝协作以完成复杂任务。

Generative AI is a very active field, and this book doesn’t aim to be a comprehensive list of available projects, runtime, or tools. The development is far from being done, with ongoing research continuously pushing the boundaries. Academia and industry are producing new papers, libraries, and projects at a rapid pace, akin to a gold rush. This section will introduce some of these technologies, focusing especially on the principles of using the Kubernetes platform to package, deploy and serve your first model.

生成式 AI 是一个非常活跃的领域，本书并不打算穷举所有可用的项目、运行时或工具。其发展远未结束，持续的研究不断推着边界前移。学术界与工业界正以淘金般的速度产出新论文、库与项目。本节将介绍其中一些技术，重点放在用 Kubernetes 平台打包、部署并服务你的第一个模型的原则上。
